56_interl1199: it is said to the women that they announce to the apostles, because through a woman death was announced, and through women life rising again
56_marg879: Bede. Peter is called by name, lest he despair because of his denial. For unless the angel had expressly named him, he who had thrice denied his master would not dare to come among the disciples. And it is to be noted why he whom the Almighty purposed to set over his Church he allowed to deny at the voice of a maidservant. For this was done by a great dispensation of mercy, so that he who was to be the shepherd of the Church might learn in his own fault how he ought to show mercy to others.
56_marg880: And Peter. He shows himself unworthy of discipleship, since he thrice denies the master. But past sins do not harm when they do not please. He goeth before you into Galilee. A brief sentence in syllogisms, but an immense promise in its scope. There is the fountain of our joy; there the origin of our eternity has been prepared. There the scattered of Israel are gathered together, and the contrite of heart are healed. There he sees him, as he said to you, not as you saw.
56_marg881: Well is it said of our Redeemer, for Galilee is interpreted ‘a transmigration made’. For he had already passed over from passion to resurrection, from death to life, from punishment to glory. And well is he seen by the disciples in Galilee after the resurrection, because we shall see the glory of his resurrection afterwards, in joy, if we too pass over from vices to the height of virtues. He who is announced in the tomb is therefore shown in the transmigration. And he who is recognized in the mortification of the flesh is seen in the transmigration of the mind.
56_marg882: Note that Mark says: “He goeth before you into Galilee; there you shall see him, as he told you”; yet he does not report that he was seen there. But Matthew says that the disciples went into Galilee, into a mountain, and there saw the Lord and adored him, and received from him the command to go, teach and baptize all nations in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. But the other evangelists teach that he had earlier been seen many times by the disciples, chiefly on the day of the resurrection in Jerusalem, and on that same day in the village of Emmaus. Why then did he foretell that he would go before them specially into Galilee, and be seen there, when he was seen neither there alone nor first? Because this voice is to be understood as spoken prophetically, not by the evangelist narrating, but by the angel at the command of the Lord, and by the Lord himself. For Galilee is called ‘transmigration’ or ‘revelation’. According to the meaning of transmigration first: what is said, “He goeth before you into Galilee; there you shall see him,” signifies that the grace of Christ was to pass over from the people of Israel to the Gentiles, by whom the apostles preaching would in no way be received, unless the Lord had prepared a way for them in their hearts; and this is “He goeth before you into Galilee.” That they, rejoicing, marvel that, every difficulty overcome, a door is opened for them in the Lord through the enlightenment of the faithful, this is “There you shall see him”; that is, there you will find his members; there you will know his living body in those who receive you. But according as Galilee is called ‘revelation’, it is to be understood not in the form of a servant, but in that form in which he is equal to the Father, who says: “I will love him, and will manifest myself to him”; not according to the way they saw him, nor even according to the way he showed himself after the resurrection to be seen and touched, with the scars; but according to ‘the ineffable light that enlightens every man that cometh into this world’, and according to ‘The light shineth in darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it.’ He went before us thither, whence coming to us he did not depart; and whither going before us he did not forsake us. For that revelation is the true Galilee: “When we shall be like to him, and shall see him as he is.” That also will be a happier passing over out of this world into that eternity, if we so embrace his precepts that we may merit to be gathered to his right hand: “Then they on the left shall go into everlasting fire, but the just into life everlasting.” Hence they shall pass over thither, and there shall see him in the way the wicked do not see him: “For the wicked is taken away, that he may not see the glory of God; and the wicked shall not see the light”; “Now this is eternal life: That they may know thee, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent”; as in that eternity it will be known whither he also leads us on account of the form of a servant, so that as free men we may behold the form of the Lord.
56_marg883: Jerome. Of the future life it is said: “Sorrow and mourning shall flee away.” The women, before the resurrection of all, imitate what they will do afterwards; that is, they are about to flee death and dread.
56_marg884: Jerome. Because only those who have merited see the mystery of the resurrection. Whence, according to John: “But Peter rising up, ran to the sepulchre,” that he might see what he had heard.
56_marg885: Mark: “And they said nothing to any man.” Luke: “And going back from the sepulchre, they told all these things to the eleven.” Matthew: “And they went out quickly from the sepulchre with fear and joy, running to tell his disciples.” But we can understand that they said nothing to any of the angels; that is, they answered nothing to those things which they had heard from them, or to the guards whom they saw lying. But the joy that Matthew speaks of does not contradict the fear of which Mark writes. For both were in their minds, but Matthew passed over the fear in silence.
56_interl1202: how and where this appearance happened, John says most fully.
56_marg886: He rose in the morning; he was buried late, that this might be fulfilled: “In the evening weeping shall have place, and in the morning gladness.” He was buried, then, on the sixth day of the sabbath, which is called Parasceve, about evening, and was placed in the tomb through the following night, and the day of the sabbath, with the following night. On the third day, that is, early on the morning of the first day of the sabbath, he rose. And well did he lie in the sepulchre one day and two nights, because he joined the light of his single death to the darkness of our double death. For we are plunged in darkness through the death of soul and spirit. Whence he brought to us his own death, that is, the death of the flesh, and loosed our two deaths: he set his single death against our double, and by dying he took away our double.
56_marg887: He is first shown to Mary Magdalen, out of whom he had cast seven devils, because harlots and publicans go before the Synagogue into the kingdom of God, as the thief went before the apostles. 56_marg888: In the beginning the woman was the author of the fault for the man; the man became the agent of error. Now she who first tasted death first sees the resurrection. And lest she bear the reproach of perpetual guilt among men, she who had transferred the fault to the man transferred grace as well. Whence she who first announced the joy of the resurrection to the mourners is recorded as healed of seven devils, so that “where sin abounded, grace did more abound” might be shown. For seven is put for the whole. But she who was freed from the seven devils, that is, from all sins, was the first to see the Lord rising, lest any who repent worthily despair of pardon, seeing her once subject to so many vices, nor as one loved by God, so that she should announce the resurrection to the evangelists and apostles themselves.
56_marg889: That the disciples believe the resurrection late is not so much their weakness as our firmness; for to the doubting the resurrection was shown by many proofs, by which we too are more firmly established.
56_marg890: Luke says this more plainly: “But their eyes were held, that they should not know him,” etc.; and afterwards: “they knew him in the breaking of the bread.” And as Luke says: “And rising up, the same hour, they went back to Jerusalem,” etc.
56_marg891: Faith labours at this, living the active life; there the contemplative life reigns in secure vision. Here we see through a mirror in an image; there we shall see the truth face to face. Whence after this: “To two of them, walking,” etc. Walking, that is labouring, he was shown in another form. And when they reported it, it was not believed, while, like Moses, they saw that it did not suffice for them. Whence Moses says: ‘Show me thyself.’ Forgetting his flesh, he asks in this life what we hope for in the future after it.
56_marg892: Luke says: “But they found the eleven gathered together, and those that were with them, saying: The Lord is risen indeed, and hath appeared.” But it is to be noted that there were some who did not believe. Whence Mark: “Neither did they believe them,” etc.

56_interl1209: that all, as witnesses, might tell all men what they together saw and heard.
56_interl1210: that belief may take its place.
56_marg893: Jerome. That a fleshy heart, full of charity, may take its place. Hence it is that bands of martyrs eagerly seek the death of this world, because they know that in exchange for temporal perishing they will live forever.
56_interl1211: Jerome. Now, after receiving the Holy Ghost, like clay vessels hardened by fire.
56_marg894: To every nation of the Gentiles. For before it had been said: “Go ye not into the way of the Gentiles,” so that the preaching of the apostles, first rejected by Judea, might then become a help to the Gentiles.
56_marg895: To the whole human race, which has something in common with every creature: with angels, with beasts, with wood, with stones, with fire and water, with the hot and the cold, the moist and the dry; because man is called ‘the lesser world’.
56_marg896: By faith which works through love.
56_marg897: Little ones believe through others, just as through others they contracted the sins which are forgiven them in baptism.
56_marg898: Is it that we do not believe if we do not work signs? But these were necessary at the beginning, so that faith might be nourished by miracles. Now that the faith of the Church is already confirmed, they are not necessary.

56_marg899: They shall cast out devils, etc. The Church does this today spiritually, when by the grace of exorcism she lays her hand on believers and drives out evil spirits.
56_marg900: They shall speak with new tongues, etc. This is done when the faithful leave behind the worldly words of their old life, and sound forth the holy mysteries, and extol the praises and power of God as far as they are able.
56_marg901: And if they shall drink any deadly thing, etc. Since they hear pestilent persuasions but do not carry them through to deeds, it therefore does not harm them if they drink the deadly thing.
56_marg902: Upon the sick, etc. While they strengthen their neighbours, confirmed in good work, by the example of good action, they lay their hands upon the sick, and they shall recover. These miracles are the greater the more spiritual they are; for by them souls are raised up, not bodies.
56_marg903: Augustine. Note that sometimes you find heavens in the plural and sometimes heaven in the singular; but in a certain abusive manner of speaking we say singular things in the plural number, and plural things in the singular. But the ‘to the east’ which the psalmist says, and the evangelists pass over in silence, signifies Jerusalem, which is situated in the parts of the east. Whence he ascended while the apostles looked on, from a land full of many miracles, where the belief of the faithful is taught more by deeds than by words.
56_marg904: And sitteth on the right hand of God, etc. Bede. And now, judging all things, he is to come at the end as judge of all. But Stephen saw him standing, because in the contest he had him as helper.
56_interl1215: the command, by obedience. Obedience is accompanied by signs.
56_marg905: Bede. Note that Mark, the later he began his gospel, the further in time he extended it by writing. For he recounts nothing of the birth of the Lord himself or of his forerunner, nor anything of the infancy or of the boyhood of either of them; nor writes anything of the Saviour’s birth, except that at the beginning of his gospel he names the Son of God. Beginning from the start of the evangelical preaching, which was done through John, he comes by narrating down to the point where the apostles sowed the same word of the gospel throughout the whole world.
